## Submission metadata

- **Conference:** Data Curation Conference 2027, Research Data Management Network, University of Basel, Thursday 14 January 2027
- **Format:** Workshop session, 75 minutes with discussion, 10:45 to 12:00, up to 20 participants
- **Presenter:** Lars Schöbitz
- **Discipline:** Global health engineering (water, sanitation and health)
- **Data curation aspect(s):** Presentation of data to humans, documentation, versioning, metadata, collaboration on GitHub, AI assisted curation with disclosure, sensitive data
- **Version:** Revised for the conference website on 10 November 2026 after the acceptance, with the agenda, the learning objectives and the prerequisites the organisers asked for, on 12 November 2026 after their comments, and reworked on 17 and 18 November 2026 after a call with the organisers (the room builds one dataset together; publishing an own dataset is offered after the workshop). The version submitted on 21 October 2026 is release v1.0.0 of the repository https://github.com/Global-Health-Engineering/workshop-dcc-2027

## Abstract

Survey and monitoring data from the water, sanitation and health sector mostly lives in spreadsheets that only their owners can read. For five years, Global Health Engineering at ETH Zurich has turned such files into published data. Each dataset becomes an R data package with a data dictionary and metadata, archived with a DOI and presented on a website with documentation and plots. AI now does most of the mechanical work. We publish for machines and humans. This workshop is about the humans, who still have to discover, interpret and trust the data.

In this workshop we build one dataset together. Every participant contributes to it through GitHub, a little before the conference and the rest in the room, and the contributions arrive as different kinds of raw data. I then run the workflow live with the free, open source tool washr, from these raw files to a data package and its website. A coding agent performs the steps. The points where a person confirms stay visible, and so does the record of what the AI did and of who contributed what. Participants review the documentation and propose changes on GitHub. In groups we then discuss four themes the workflow raises for data curation: oversight of AI curation, disclosure of AI contributions, sensitive data, and scientific credit for data.

Participants who could imagine publishing a dataset of their own this way can tell me after the workshop, and I follow up with them.

## Agenda

- 15 min: Introduction, why we publish for humans and the workflow in one picture
- 35 min: Building a dataset together, from the raw contributions to the data package and its website
- 20 min: Discussion in four groups, one theme each
- 5 min: Take home

## Learning objectives

Participants will be able to:

- Describe the stages a raw dataset passes through on its way to a published data package and website.
- Contribute to a shared dataset on GitHub with issues and comments, and propose a change that way.
- Tell which steps of data curation a coding agent can take over, which stay with the researcher, and how AI contributions are recorded.

## Prerequisites

- Bring your own laptop. No software has to be installed.
- A free GitHub account. The workshop website explains how to create one.
- By Friday 8 January 2027: take the pre-course survey and make your first contribution to the workshop dataset on GitHub. The workshop website explains both: <https://rawtoweb.github.io/website/dcc-2027/>
